slot.brief: Two lines in space given in symmetric form; use the determinant/coplanarity test to check whether they intersect.

verdicts.working: Direction vectors are (1,2,1) and (2,1,-1), so the lines are not parallel. Equating coordinates gives inconsistent equations, so they do not intersect; hence they are skew.

working:
$\mathbf d_1=(1,2,1),\quad \mathbf d_2=(2,1,-1),\quad \mathbf B-\mathbf A=(2,2,1)$.
$(\mathbf B-\mathbf A)\cdot(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2)=(2,2,1)\cdot(-3,3,-3)=-3\ne0$.
$\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2\ne\mathbf0$; the lines are nonparallel and noncoplanar, hence skew. Independent check: Direction vectors are (1,2,1) and (2,1,-1), so the lines are not parallel. Equating coordinates gives inconsistent equations, so they do not intersect; hence they are skew.
